369	## Debug
370	
371	| Error | Cause | Fix |
372	| --- | --- | --- |
373	| Node type not found in registry | Model not published, or registry cache stale | Run `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
374	| `model.context` rejected by runtime | `folderKey` or `modelName` missing from `inputs` (the context array is built from these) | Confirm `inputs.modelName` and `inputs.folderKey` are populated. |
375	| Empty `$vars.{nodeId}.output` | Model's taxonomy doesn't match the document, or extraction silently returned no fields | Inspect the raw API response via `$vars.{nodeId}.error` first; if no error, run the extraction against the same document on the IxP product UI to compare |
376	| `fileRef` not resolving | Expression references an upstream variable that isn't wired, or the upstream node didn't produce a file output | Verify the upstream node exports a file reference and that the `=js:$vars.{upstreamId}.output.<field>` expression matches |
377	| `[430002] Invalid input on document extraction operation` at debug | `fileRef` bound to the attachment's `.ID` (or another scalar) instead of the attachment object — `flow validate` does not catch this | Bind the whole object: `=js:$vars.<upstream>.output.<attachment>` — drop the `.ID` |
378	| `[430002] Invalid input on document extraction operation` at debug, backend detail `'downloadedFileOutput' is missing the required 'ID' field` | The `fileRef` expression is correct, but the source flow input is declared `"type": "object"` instead of `"type": "file"` — the attachment has nowhere to bind, so the variable holds a plain JSON object | Declare the input `type: "file"`. See [Wiring `fileRef`](#wiring-fileref--file-variable-bound-to-the-trigger). |
379	| Extraction failed | Underlying IxP model errored (unsupported MIME type, corrupted file, service-side failure) | Check `$vars.{nodeId}.error.detail` for the IxP service response |
380	| `uip maestro flow node configure` rejects with "not a connector type node" | Expected — IxP is not a connector. | Edit `inputs.*` in the `.flow` JSON directly. |
381	| Studio Web: "Cannot destructure property 'modelName' of 't' as it is undefined" when clicking the node | `inputs.model` blob is missing or undefined. The `schema-definition` form section binds `inputs.model` to the `ixp-model-taxonomy` component, which destructures `modelName` and `folderKey` out of it. When `inputs.model` is missing, the destructure throws. | Copy `definition.inputDefaults.model` verbatim into the node instance's `inputs.model`. The blob carries `id`, `modelName`, `modelDisplayName`, `folderKey`, `folderName`, `folderPath`, `description`. See [JSON Structure](#json-structure). |
382	| `flow validate` error `inputs.model must be an object with non-empty string modelName and folderKey` | `inputDefaults.model.modelName` was `null` (common for published/OOB deployments) and copied verbatim into `inputs.model`. | Set `inputs.model.modelName` from `inputDefaults.model.modelDisplayName` (Authoring rule #1). `folderKey` is normally populated in the blob; if it too is empty, take it from the flat `inputDefaults.folderKey`. |
383

1	# IxP Extraction Node — Planning
2	
3	IxP Extraction nodes invoke a **trained, published** UiPath Intelligent eXtraction Platform (IxP) model to pull structured fields out of unstructured or semi-structured documents (PDFs, photos, scanned forms). They are tenant-specific resources that appear in the registry after `uip login` + `uip maestro flow registry pull`.
4	
5	In the IxP product these published models are also called **runtime projects** — the bundle published to the tenant runtime and callable from a flow. Treat "what IxP models do I have", "what runtime projects do I have access to in flow", and "list published extractors" as the same listing question — see [Listing Available Models / Runtime Projects](#listing-available-models--runtime-projects).
6	
7	## Node Type Pattern
8	
9	`uipath.ixp.{modelName}.{fullyQualifiedName}`
10	
11	Unlike other resource plugins that use the `uipath.core.*` prefix, IxP nodes use `uipath.ixp.*` and a **two-segment tail**: `{modelName}` is the model's display name, and `{fullyQualifiedName}` is the model's fully-qualified name on the tenant (e.g. `Shared/invoice-model`). Both segments are sanitized — see [impl.md](impl.md) for the rule and concrete examples. Model versioning is a separate input field (`versionTag`), not part of the node type.
12	
13	## When to Use
14	
15	Use an IxP node when the flow needs to extract **named fields** (invoice totals, contract parties, receipt line items, form values) from documents whose **layout varies across inputs** and which are not already machine-readable.
16	
17	### IxP vs Script/Connector/HTTP/Agent Decision Table
18	
19	| Use an IxP node when... | Use something else when... |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| Source is a PDF, scanned document, photo, or email attachment | Source is already structured (CSV, JSON, database row) — use [Script](../script/planning.md) |
22	| Fields have variable layout across documents (e.g. invoices from many vendors) | Layout is fixed and parseable by regex/XPath — use [Script](../script/planning.md) |
23	| A trained IxP model exists for this document type | No model exists — flag as a prerequisite and use `core.logic.mock` until the model is trained |
24	| Need field-level extraction with per-field confidence scores for downstream HITL review | Need free-form summarization, classification, or reasoning over text — use [Agent](../agent/planning.md) |
25	
26	### Anti-Pattern
27	
28	Don't use IxP as a generic OCR. IxP is field-oriented — it extracts named fields against a trained taxonomy. Running IxP to get raw text back and then parsing the text downstream throws away the part of IxP that's actually valuable.
29	
30	### When NOT to Use
31	
32	- **Model not yet trained or published** — use `core.logic.mock` and surface in Open Questions that a model must be trained on the IxP product before the flow can run.
33	- **Structured input (CSV/JSON/DB row)** — use [Script](../script/planning.md) or [Decision](../decision/planning.md). IxP adds latency and model-inference cost for no gain.
34	- **Free-form summarization, classification, or reasoning** — use [Agent](../agent/planning.md). An IxP model trained for field extraction will not produce useful output for those tasks.
35	- **Manual external API call** — use [Connector](../connector/planning.md) or [HTTP](../http/planning.md).
36	
37	## Prerequisites
38	
39	- `uip login` — IxP nodes only appear in the registry after authentication.
40	- `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` must be run to cache IxP model node types locally.
41	- A trained, published IxP extraction model must exist on the tenant. If none exists, surface it in the **Open Questions** section of the architectural plan so the user can train one while reviewing.
42	
43	## Ports
44	
45	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `input` | `success`, `error` (the visible `error` port / edge target is gated by `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled`; the `outputs.error` schema entry on the node instance is always required — see [impl.md Authoring rule #4](impl.md#authoring-rules)) |
48	
49	## Output Variables
50	
51	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — the extraction-result object directly. The BPMN serializer maps the service's `result` field with `source: '=result'`, so **the `result` wrapper is stripped** at runtime. Top-level keys: `ExtractionResult`, `ExtractorPayloads`, `BusinessrulesResults`. Field-level values live under `output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields[]` / `Tables[]`; exact field names depend on the trained model's taxonomy. See [impl.md — Accessing Output](impl.md#accessing-output) for the canonical access path.
52	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — populated when the `error` port is wired and extraction fails. Mapped from the IxP service response's `Error` field (`source: '=Error'`) — see [impl.md — Accessing Output](impl.md#accessing-output).
53	
54	## Discovery
55	
56	```bash
57	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
58	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp" --output json
59	```
60	
61	Requires `uip login`. Only published IxP models from your tenant appear. The returned node type uses a **two-segment tail** (`{modelName}.{fullyQualifiedName}`), unlike `uipath.core.*` siblings which use a single-segment tail. Both tail segments are sanitized: lowercase, then runs of any character outside `[a-z0-9]` → single `-`. So an FQN of `Shared/invoice-model` lands as `shared-invoice-model`. See [impl.md](impl.md) for the full rule and worked examples.
62	
63	### If `Data: []` → plan for a mock + Open Question
64	
65	If the search returns no `uipath.ixp.*` nodes, no IxP extraction model is published on this tenant. Plan the architecture around a `core.logic.mock` placeholder for the extraction step, and surface the missing model in **Open Questions** so the user can train and publish it. Do not iterate on registry searches — the mock is the planning answer until the model exists. See [impl.md — If the Model Does Not Exist Yet](impl.md#if-the-model-does-not-exist-yet) for the implementer-side procedure.
66	
67	## Listing Available Models / Runtime Projects
68	
69	Q&A use case from a Maestro-flow context: user asks "what IxP models can I access in Maestro?", "what IxP models / runtime projects can I use in this flow?", "what document extractors can I add here?", "which document extractors are published?". Answer from the `uipath-maestro-flow` Skill via the flow registry — do not switch to the `uipath-ixp` Skill (`uip ixp projects ...` enumerates IxP-product projects, not what is published into the Maestro registry).
70	
71	Read-only listing — **do not** scaffold a solution, init a flow, or write a `.flow` file:
72	
73	1. Confirm `uip login status --output json`. Without login, only OOTB nodes are returned and tenant IxP models will not appear.
74	2. Refresh the cache and search:
75	   ```bash
76	   uip maestro flow registry pull --force
77	   uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp" --output json
78	   ```
79	3. Format `Data[]` as a table — `DisplayName`, `NodeType`, `Version`. Each entry is one published model / runtime project. See [impl.md — Listing Published Models](impl.md#listing-published-models) for parsing details.
80	
81	Search term must be `"uipath.ixp"` (lowercase). Do NOT use `"runtime"`, `"document extractor"`, `"extractor"`, or `"IXP"` — these miss extraction nodes.
82	
83	If `Data: []`, answer directly that no IxP models are published on the tenant. Do not propose a `core.logic.mock` workaround — the mock is for build-time planning, not for listing-time Q&A.
84	
85	## Planning Annotation
86	
87	In the architectural plan:
88	
89	- If the model exists: note as `resource: <model-name> (ixp-extraction)` with the intended document type (e.g. "resource: vendor-invoices (ixp-extraction) — extract invoice header + line items")
90	- If it does not exist: note as `[CREATE NEW] <description>` and flag in Open Questions that an IxP model must be trained before the flow can run
91

1	# HITL Node — Implementation
2	
3	Two node types implement human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Choose based on whether you need an inline form or an existing deployed app.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Option 1 — `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (Inline Schema — OOTB)
8	
9	This is the preferred option. No registry pull, no app publishing, no tenant dependency. Write the node directly into the `.flow` file as JSON.
10	
11	**Full implementation guide, JSON examples, and schema conversion rules:**
12	→ [`uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill — hitl-node-quickform.md](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-quickform.md)
13	
14	> **Note:** Skills are self-contained. This cross-skill reference is for documentation context only. The agent uses the `uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill to implement HITL nodes. This implementation guide is for implementation-phase topology resolution only — not for schema design or node writing.
15	
16	### Adding / Editing
17	
18	For add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). **Use `Edit` / `Write` for HITL node authoring.** Do not use the dedicated HITL CLI for this non-carve-out structural edit. Wire the `outcome-completed` port after adding the node.
19	
20	### Quick Reference
21	
22	**Node JSON (minimum viable):**
23	
24	```json
25	{
26	  "id": "hitlReview1",
27	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form",
28	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
29	  "display": { "label": "Invoice Review" },
30	  "inputs": {
31	    "schema": {
32	      "schemaId": "<uuid>",
33	      "fields": [
34	        { "id": "invoiceid", "label": "Invoice ID", "type": "text",   "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice.output.invoiceId" },
35	        { "id": "amount",    "label": "Amount",     "type": "number", "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice.output.amount" },
36	        { "id": "decision",  "label": "Decision",   "type": "text",   "direction": "output", "variable": "vars.decision" }
37	      ],
38	      "outcomes": [
39	        { "id": "approve", "name": "Approve", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true,  "action": "Continue" },
40	        { "id": "reject",  "name": "Reject",  "type": "string", "isPrimary": false, "action": "End" }
41	      ]
42	    },
43	    "recipient": { "channels": ["Email", "ActionCenter"], "connections": {}, "assignee": { "type": "group" } },
44	    "priority": "Low"
45	  },
46	  "outputs": {
47	    "output": {
48	      "type": "object",
49	      "description": "Task result data",
50	      "source": "=result",
51	      "var": "output",
52	      "properties": {
53	        "decision": { "type": "string" },
54	        "Action":   { "type": "string", "enum": ["Approve", "Reject"], "default": "Approve" }
55	      }
56	    },
57	    "status": {
58	      "type": "string",
59	      "description": "Task completion status",
60	      "source": "=result.Action",
61	      "var": "status",
62	      "enum": ["Approve", "Reject"],
63	      "default": "Approve"
64	    }
65	  }
66	}
67	```
68	
69	**Field format rules:**
70	- **Input fields**: `binding: "vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>"` (raw path, no `=js:$` prefix). No `variable` property on input fields.
71	- **Output fields**: `variable: "vars.<globalName>"` (`vars.` prefix required). No `binding`.
72	- **InOut fields**: both `binding` and `variable`, same formats as above.
73	- `schemaId` (not `id`) at the schema level — generate a fresh UUID.
74	- `typeVersion` — always `"1.0"` for `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`. **Do not run `registry get` to derive this value; do not use `"1.1"` or any other version.** The OOTB HITL node version is stable at `1.0`.
75	- No `model` block on node instances — only the definition carries it.
76	
77	**outputs block**: only `output` (with `properties` for output/inOut fields + `Action` outcome) and `status` (with `enum`/`default` from outcomes). No per-field `custom: true` entries.
78	
79	**Ports:** `input` (target) → `outcome-completed` (source, label: Completed)
80	
81	**Output variables:**
82	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — object with all `output` / `inOut` field values, keyed by **field `id`**
83	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldId}` — individual field value (e.g. `$vars.hitlReview1.output.decision`)
84	- `$vars.{nodeId}.status` — selected outcome name (e.g. `"Approve"`, `"Reject"`)
85	- `$vars.{globalId}` — workflow-global alias; `globalId` is `field.variable` with `vars.` stripped. **Do not use this in scripts — always use `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldId}` instead.**
86	
87	---

89	## Option 2 — App-Based HITL (`uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app`)
90	
91	Use when there is an existing deployed Action Center app that should serve as the task form.
92	
93	### Discovery
94	
95	**CLI (primary path):**
96	
97	```bash
98	uip solution resources list --kind App --output json
99	```
100	
101	Returns all Action Center app types (`vB Action`, `workflow Action`, `Coded Action`, `JS Action`). Filter by app name. Then retrieve the configuration:
102	
103	```bash
104	uip solution resources get <key> --output json
105	```
106	
107	**Direct API fallback (if CLI unavailable):**
108	
109	```
110	GET {BASE_URL}/{ORG}/studio_/backend/api/resourcebuilder/solutions/{SOLUTION_ID}/resources/search
111	  ?kind=app&pageSize=25&projectKey={PROJECT_KEY}&includeSolutionResources=true
112	  &types=VB%20Action&types=Workflow%20Action&types=Coded%20Action&types=CodedAction&types=JS%20Action

114	
115	Full step-by-step (app search → retrieve-configuration → resource files → reference registration → debug overwrites) → **[hitl-node-apptask.md](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-apptask.md)**
116	
117	### Node JSON (Quick Reference)
118	
119	```json
120	{
121	  "id": "invoiceReview1",
122	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app",
123	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
124	  "display": { "label": "Invoice Review" },
125	  "inputs": {
126	    "recipient": { "channels": ["ActionCenter"], "connections": {}, "assignee": { "type": "group" } },
127	    "app": {
128	      "displayName": "Invoice Approval",
129	      "name": "Invoice Approval",
130	      "key": "<app.key>",
131	      "folderPath": "Shared",
132	      "inputSchema": {
133	        "type": "object",
134	        "properties": {
135	          "<paramName>": { "type": "string" }
136	        }
137	      },
138	      "outputSchema": {
139	        "type": "object",
140	        "properties": {
141	          "<outputName>": { "type": "string" }
142	        }
143	      }
144	    },
145	    "appInputBindings": {
146	      "<inputParamName>": "=vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>",
147	      "<inputParamName2>": "=metadata.InstanceId"
148	    },
149	    "schema": {
150	      "fields": [],
151	      "outcomes": [{ "id": "submit", "name": "Submit", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true, "action": "Continue" }]
152	    },
153	    "priority": "Medium"
154	  },
155	  "outputs": {
156	    "output": {
157	      "type": "object",
158	      "description": "Task result data",
159	      "source": "=result",
160	      "var": "output",
161	      "properties": {
162	        "Action": { "type": "string", "enum": ["Submit"], "default": "Submit" }
163	      }
164	    },
165	    "status": {
166	      "type": "string",
167	      "description": "Task completion status",
168	      "source": "=result.Action",

171	      "default": "Submit"

173	  }
174	}

176	
177	**`typeVersion`** — fill in the version returned by `uip maestro flow registry get <appKey>` for the specific deployed app. Unlike QuickForm (always `"1.0"`), AppTask version varies per app definition.

179	**`inputs.app`**: `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` are JSON Schema objects (`{ "type": "object", "properties": { ... } }`), **not arrays**.
180	
181	**`inputs.appInputBindings`** — maps app input parameter names to binding expressions. Format: `"=vars.<path>"` (with `=` prefix, no `js:`). Key = parameter name from `inputSchema.properties`. Without this, all input fields appear blank.

183	### If the app does not exist yet
184

189	## Common Pattern — Human-in-the-Loop
190	
191	```text
192	Manual Trigger -> RPA Process (extract) -> HITL (review) -> Decision (approved?) ->
193	  true: Script (submit) -> End
194	  false: End
195	```
196	
197	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <ProjectName>.flow` reports an unwired completion port before you publish; it accepts both the `outcome-completed` spelling used here and the `completed` spelling used in [planning-arch.md](../../planning-arch.md#standard-port-reference) and the failure catalog.

199	## Debug
200	
201	| Error | Cause | Fix |
202	| --- | --- | --- |
203	| Node type not found in registry (Option 2) | App not published or registry stale | If in same solution: `uip maestro flow registry list --local`. Otherwise: `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
204	| Task never completes | Human hasn't submitted the form | Check task assignment in Orchestrator |
205	| Output missing expected fields | App form doesn't match expected schema | Verify app form fields match what the flow expects |
206	| `outcome-completed` port unwired (Option 1) | Missing edge on output handle | Wire the `outcome-completed` output handle — an unwired `outcome-completed` blocks the flow indefinitely |

1	# HITL Node — Planning
2	
3	The flow needs to pause for a human to review, approve, or fill in data. Two node types serve this need — choose based on form complexity and whether an app already exists.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Which HITL Node to Use
8	
9	| Use case | Node type | Form source |
10	| --- | --- | --- |
11	| Inline form designed right now (fields + outcomes defined in the flow) | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` | Schema embedded in node inputs — no app needed |
12	| Existing coded app or Action Center app | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app` | Deployed app from Orchestrator |
13	
14	**Prefer `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`** for new flows. It is an OOTB node — no registry discovery, no app publishing, no tenant dependency.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Option 1 — `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (Inline Schema — OOTB)
19	
20	Node type: `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`
21	Available: always — no `uip login` or registry pull required.
22	
23	### When to Select
24	
25	| Situation | Select? |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Manager approval before processing | Yes |
28	| Human reviews extracted data before submission | Yes |
29	| Human resolves exceptions the automation cannot handle | Yes |
30	| Need a quick form with specific fields and outcomes | Yes |
31	| Existing coded/Action Center app should be used | No — use Option 2 |
32	| Fully automated processing, no human involvement | No |
33	
34	### Ports
35	
36	| Input port | Output port |
37	| --- | --- |
38	| `input` | `outcome-completed` |
39	
40	**The output port must be wired.** A node with no edge on `outcome-completed` blocks the flow indefinitely.
41	
42	### Output Variables
43	
44	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — object containing all output and inOut fields the human filled in
45	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldName}` — individual field value
46	- `$vars.{nodeId}.status` — selected outcome's action value (`"Continue"` or `"End"`)
47	
48	### Schema Design
49	
50	The schema defines what the human sees and provides. Three field categories:
51	
52	| Category | Human can… | Use for |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| `inputs` | Read only | Context the human needs to decide |
55	| `outputs` | Write | Data the automation needs back |
56	| `inOuts` | Read + modify | Fields the human can see and optionally correct |
57	
58	Outcomes are the action buttons (e.g., Approve/Reject). First outcome is primary.
59	
60	**In the architectural plan**, describe the schema:
61	```
62	inputs:   [invoiceId (string), amount (number)]
63	outputs:  [decision (string, required)]
64	outcomes: [Approve, Reject]
65	priority: Low
66	```
67	
68	Full JSON format and conversion examples: see [`uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-quickform.md).
69	
70	> **Note:** Skills are self-contained — cross-skill references are for documentation context only. The agent uses the `uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill to implement HITL nodes; this planning guide is for topology selection only.
71	
72	### Wiring Pattern
73	
74	```
75	[Upstream] -> [HITL] ->|outcome-completed| [Continue]
76	```
77	
78	### Common Topology Patterns
79	
80	**Approval gate:**
81	```
82	Trigger -> Fetch Data -> HITL (review) ->|outcome-completed| Decision (approved?) ->
83	  true: Script (process) -> End
84	  false: Script (log rejection) -> End
85	```
86	
87	**Exception escalation:**
88	```
89	Trigger -> Process -> Decision (confidence ok?) ->
90	  true: Continue -> End
91	  false: HITL (exception review) ->|outcome-completed| Script (retry with human input) -> End
92	```
93	
94	### Planning Annotation
95	
96	In the node table:
97	```
98	| hitlReview | Invoice Review | human-task | uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form | inputs: [invoiceId, amount] outputs: [decision] outcomes: [Approve, Reject] | output, status |
99	```
100	
101	---
102	
103	## Option 2 — `uipath.core.human-task.{key}` (App-Based)
104	
105	Node type: `uipath.core.human-task.{key}`
106	Available: tenant-specific resource — requires `uip login` + `uip maestro flow registry pull`.
107	
108	### When to Select
109	
110	Use when there is an existing coded app or Action Center app that should be the task form.
111	
112	### Ports
113	
114	| Input port | Output port |
115	| --- | --- |
116	| `input` | `output` |
117	
118	### Output Variables
119	
120	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — form data submitted by the user
121	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if execution fails
122	
123	### Discovery
124	
125	**Published (tenant registry):**
126	
127	```bash
128	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
129	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.human-task" --output json
130	```
131	
132	**In-solution (local, no login required):**
133	
134	```bash
135	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
136	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json
137	```
138	
139	Run from inside the flow project directory. Discovers sibling projects in the same `.uipx` solution.
140	
141	### Planning Annotation
142	
143	- If the app exists: note as `resource: <name> (human-task)`
144	- If it does not exist: note as `[CREATE NEW] <description>` with skill `uipath-coded-apps`, use `core.logic.mock` placeholder

1	# Connector Trigger Nodes — Implementation
2	
3	How to configure connector trigger nodes: connection binding, enriched metadata, event parameter resolution, and trigger-specific `node configure` fields. This replaces the IS activity workflow (Steps 1-6 in [connector/impl.md](../connector/impl.md)) — trigger nodes have different metadata and configuration.
4	
5	> **This plugin covers two node families that share the same configuration mechanism:**
6	>
7	> - **Connector triggers** (`uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>`) — start node; the event starts the flow. The default subject of every step below.
8	> - **Wait for events** (`uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>`) — a mid-flow event node; the flow pauses and waits for the event before continuing. Same connection binding, enriched metadata, event parameter resolution, filter trees, and `node configure` fields. Only the placement and node lifecycle differ. See [Wait for events](#wait-for-events-uipathconnectoreventkeyevent) for the deltas, then apply Steps 1-6 below unchanged.
9	
10	## Configuration Workflow
11	
12	Follow these steps for every IS trigger node.
13	
14	### Step 1 — Fetch a preliminary connection and query trigger objects
15	
16	Extract the connector key from the node type (`uipath.connector.trigger.<connector-key>.<trigger-name>`) and the operation name from the `registry get` response (`model.context[].operation`).
17	
18	**1a. Get any enabled connection** — needed as `--connection-id` for `triggers objects` below.
19	
20	Discovery call is **always**:
21	
22	```bash
23	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
24	```
25	
26	`--all-folders` is mandatory. Without it the CLI returns the active folder only and hides connections in other folders the user can see. Plain `uip is connections list "<connector-key>"` is forbidden for discovery.
27	
28	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md). Single source of truth for selection rules, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, ping verification.
29	
30	Pick any enabled connection (prefer `IsDefault: Yes`) and capture its `Id` for Step 1b.
31	
32	**1b. Query trigger objects** — **mandatory** for every trigger node. Do NOT skip:
33	
34	```bash
35	uip is triggers objects "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" \
36	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
37	```
38	
39	Save the response. It carries three pieces per event object that drive later steps:
40	
41	| Field | Drives | Meaning |
42	|------|--------|---------|
43	| `byoaConnection` | Step 1c | If `true`, only BYOA connections are valid for this event |
44	| `isWebhookUrlVisible` | Step 6b | If `true`, retrieve and present the webhook URL |
45	| **`parameters[]`** | Steps 3 & 4 | Object-, query-, and path-scoped input parameters (e.g. shared mailbox, repo, owner). **NOT the complete event-parameter set** — merge with `EventParameters` from `triggers describe` (Step 1b-2). The full input set is the **union** of both; a field is required if either source marks it `required`. |
46	
47	It may also include `design.textBlocks` with connector-specific user-facing instructions (e.g., "Add this URL to your Slack app's Event Subscriptions"). Surface that text verbatim when applicable — do not invent service-specific guidance.
48	
49	> `byoaConnection` and `isWebhookUrlVisible` are per event object, not per connector — some connectors require BYOA for some events but not others. `parameters[]` is per event object too: each operation has its own input fields.
50	
51	#### Reading `parameters[]`
52	
53	Each entry is one input field the user supplies when configuring the trigger (e.g., GitHub `repo`, Outlook `parentFolderId`, Slack `channelId`). For each:
54	
55	| Key | Use |
56	|---|---|
57	| `name` | Key inside the `--detail` bucket selected by `type` — see below |
58	| `displayName` | Label when prompting the user for a missing value |
59	| `dataType` | Value type (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, …) |
60	| `required` | Drives Step 4's required-field check |
61	| `reference` | Present → resolve to an ID in Step 3 (`uip is resources run list`) before configure |
62	| `description` | Field hint — surface verbatim when prompting |
63	| `design.position` | `"primary"` indicates a top-level input field; other positions are layout hints — safe to ignore for configure |
64	| `type` | Bucket selector in Step 6's `--detail`: `"query"` → `queryParameters`, `"path"` → `pathParameters`, else → `eventParameters` |
65	
66	> **Source of truth — the UNION of two calls, never one alone.** The complete event-input set = `triggers objects → parameters[]` (object/query/path scope) **∪** `triggers describe → EventParameters` (event-config scope). Configure every field that **either** marks `required: true`. `triggers describe → FilterFields` feeds the `filter` tree; `OutputFields` / `outputResponseDefinition` feed downstream `$vars`. `flow registry get`'s `eventParameters.fields` mirrors `describe` and is the offline fallback. A required field can appear in `describe → EventParameters` while absent from `parameters[]`, so **both calls are mandatory and you must merge them**. Full field semantics: [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md — `parameters[]`](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#parameters--event-parameter-input-fields).
67	
68	**1b-2. Resolve the object name and fetch field metadata** — **mandatory** for every trigger node.
69	
70	> **MUST READ before this step:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md). Single source of truth for fetching trigger parameters and fields — object name resolution, describe call, source-of-truth contract.
71	
72	1. Resolve `<objectName>` from the Step 1b `triggers objects` response per [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md — Object Name Resolution](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#object-name-resolution). If the object name is not recognizable from the user's prompt, **ask the user** — present candidates by `displayName`. Do NOT guess.
73	2. Fetch field metadata:
74	
75	```bash
76	uip is triggers describe "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" "<objectName>" \
77	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
78	```
79	
80	> **Source of truth for node configuration — merge both responses.** Event-parameter inputs = the **union** of `triggers objects → parameters[]` (Step 1b) and `triggers describe → EventParameters` (this step). `triggers describe` also returns `FilterFields` (→ `filter` tree) and `OutputFields` (→ downstream `$vars`). Never treat `triggers describe` as "only field metadata" — its `EventParameters` are first-class event parameters and frequently carry required fields that `parameters[]` omits. Do NOT skip this call, and do NOT invent parameters or fields.
81	
82	### Step 1c — Select the final connection
83	
84	**If `byoaConnection: true`** — the Step 1a connection is not usable. Follow the BYOA selection workflow in [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md — For BYOA Connections](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md#for-byoa-connections-webhook-triggers) (filter with `--byoa`, `--refresh` retry, stop-and-ask if none exist).
85	
86	**If `byoaConnection: false`** — use the Step 1a connection. Verify health:
87	
88	```bash
89	uip is connections ping "<connection-id>" --output json
90	```
91	
92	### Step 2 — Get enriched trigger metadata
93	
94	`--connection-id` is **required** for trigger nodes. Without it, the command fails.
95	
96	```bash
97	uip maestro flow registry get <trigger-node-type> --connection-id <connection-id> --output json
98	```
99	
100	The response contains three trigger-specific sections:
101	
102	**`eventParameters.fields`** — non-authoritative. Often empty (see Step 1b). Iterate [`parameters[]`](#reading-parameters) from Step 1b in Steps 3 and 4 — do not iterate this block.
103	
104	Shape only — do not iterate:
105	
106	```json
107	{
108	  "eventParameters": {
109	    "fields": [
110	      {
111	        "name": "parentFolderId",
112	        "displayName": "Email folder",
113	        "type": "string",
114	        "required": true,
115	        "reference": {
116	          "objectName": "MailFolder",
117	          "lookupValue": "id",
118	          "lookupNames": ["displayName"],
119	          "path": "/MailFolders"
120	        }
121	      }
122	    ]
123	  }
124	}
125	```
126	
127	**`filterFields`** — fields used to narrow *which* events fire the trigger (e.g., only emails from a specific sender). These are optional filter criteria and are passed as a structured tree in `--detail.filter` (see [Filter Trees](#filter-trees)).
128	
129	```json
130	{
131	  "filterFields": {
132	    "fields": [
133	      {
134	        "name": "fromAddress",
135	        "displayName": "From address",
136	        "type": "string",
137	        "required": false
138	      }
139	    ]
140	  }
141	}
142	```
143	
144	**`outputResponseDefinition`** — the event payload schema (all fields the trigger outputs when it fires). **Save this** — you need it in Step 4b to know the exact field paths for downstream `$vars` expressions (e.g., `$vars.{nodeId}.output.text`, `$vars.{nodeId}.output.channel`). Do not guess output field names.
145	
146	**`eventMode`** — `"webhooks"` or `"polling"`.
147	
148	The response (which becomes the `definitions[]` entry verbatim) includes `model.context` with:
149	- `connectorKey` — the connector identifier
150	- `operation` — the event operation name (e.g., `"EMAIL_RECEIVED"`, `"ISSUE_CREATED"`)
151	- `objectName` — the IS object (e.g., `"Message"`, `"Issue"`)
152	
153	These live in the **definition**, not on the node instance. The instance carries only `inputs` (event filter fields) and `outputs`.
154	
155	### Step 3 — Resolve reference fields in event parameters
156	
157	Iterate the **union** of `parameters[]` (Step 1b) and `EventParameters` (Step 1b-2). For each entry with a `reference` key, run an ID lookup — same mechanism as IS activity nodes. A referenced field can live in `describe → EventParameters` while absent from `parameters[]` — resolving only `parameters[]` misses it.
158	
159	> **Resolve every reference field freshly, against the current `--connection-id`, immediately before `node configure` (Step 6)** — even if you think you already know the ID from a previous flow. Reference IDs are connection-scoped and reused values fault silently at runtime. See [Reference IDs Are Connection-Scoped (CRITICAL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#reference-ids-are-connection-scoped-critical) for the full mechanism and failure mode, and the top-level Anti-Patterns in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
160	
161	```bash
162	# Example: resolve Outlook mail folder "Inbox" to its ID
163	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<reference.objectName>" \
164	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
165	```
166	
167	The `<id>` in `--connection-id "<id>"` MUST be the connection bound to **this** flow (the final connection from Step 1c), not any other connection you've used in another flow. Use the resolved IDs — from this very `run list` call — in the trigger's event parameter configuration.
168	
169	> **Paginate when looking up by name.** Use `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` with `--query "nextPage=<token>"`. Short-circuit on match. Do NOT conclude "not found" until `HasMore` is `"false"`. See [resources.md#pagination](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md#pagination).
170	
171	**Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — Integration Service — resources.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) for the full reference-resolution workflow** (pagination, describe failures, fallbacks).
172	
173	### Step 4 — Validate required event parameters
174	
175	Check every entry in the **union** of `parameters[]` (Step 1b) and `EventParameters` (Step 1b-2). Treat a field as required if **either** source marks `required: true`. All required event parameters must have values before building the flow.
176	
177	1. Collect all required entries from `parameters[]` **and** `describe → EventParameters` (dedupe by `name`); required = required in either
178	2. For each, check if the user's prompt provides a value
179	3. If any required field is missing, **ask the user** — list the missing fields with their `displayName` (and `description` if useful). Free-form input is appropriate when the value space is open-ended; when a finite set of sensible values exists, present them as options per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
180	4. Only proceed after all required event parameters are resolved
181	
182	> Step 6 buckets each resolved value into `eventParameters`, `queryParameters`, or `pathParameters` based on the entry's `type` — see Step 6's `--detail` table.
183	
184	### Step 4b — Map trigger output fields for downstream nodes
185	
186	Before wiring downstream nodes, check `outputResponseDefinition` from Step 2 to know the exact field names available in `$vars.{triggerId}.output`. Do NOT guess field names — different triggers output different schemas.
187	
188	Each trigger type has a different output schema — field names like `.text`, `.subject`, or `.body.content` vary by connector. Use the actual field names from `outputResponseDefinition` when writing expressions in downstream nodes.
189	
190	### Step 5 — Replace the manual trigger with the connector trigger node
191	
192	Follow the [CLI: Replace manual trigger with connector trigger](../../editing-operations-cli.md#replace-manual-trigger-with-connector-trigger) procedure. The CLI handles edge cleanup, orphaned definition removal, and `variables.nodes` regeneration automatically. Note the generated node ID from the `node add` response — you need it for Step 6.
193	
194	### Step 6 — Configure the trigger node
195	
196	> **MUST READ before `node configure`:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md). The parameters fetched there (`triggers objects` → `parameters[]`, Step 1b) and fields (`triggers describe`, Step 1b-2) are the source of truth for everything in `--detail`. If you have not run both calls, go back to Step 1b.
197	
198	**Read the `--detail` field table below before calling `node configure`.** The fields and types are strict — unknown keys or wrong types cause validation errors. Do not guess field names from other node types (e.g., activity nodes use `method`/`endpoint`/`bodyParameters`; triggers use `eventMode`/`eventParameters`/`filter`, plus `objectName` for generic triggers).
199	
200	Use `node configure` with trigger-specific `--detail` fields:
201	
202	```bash
203	uip maestro flow node configure <PROJECT>.flow <triggerId> --output json --detail '{
204	  "connectionId": "<CONNECTION_ID>",
205	  "folderKey": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
206	  "eventMode": "<EVENT_MODE>",
207	  "objectName": "<OBJECT_NAME>",
208	  "eventParameters": { "<paramName>": "<RESOLVED_VALUE>" },
209	  "filter": {
210	    "groupOperator": 0,
211	    "index": 0,
212	    "filters": [
213	      {
214	        "id": "subject",
215	        "operator": "Contains",
216	        "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true }
217	      }
218	    ]
219	  }
220	}'
221	```
222	
223	**`--detail` fields for triggers:**
224	
225	| Field | Required | Description |
226	|---|---|---|
227	| `connectionId` | Yes | Connection UUID from Step 1c (the final connection — BYOA if required) |
228	| `folderKey` | Yes | Orchestrator folder key for the connection |
229	| `eventMode` | Yes | `"webhooks"` or `"polling"` — from `registry get` response |
230	| `objectName` | Generic triggers only | The IS object the event subscribes to (e.g. the Data Fabric entity name) — the object name resolved in Step 1b-2. **Required for generic triggers** (`activityType: "GenericTrigger"` in the definition's `connectorDetail.configuration` — one manifest templated across every object, so its `objectName` context entry ships empty). **Omit for curated triggers** (`activityType: "CuratedTrigger"`) — the manifest's baked-in objectName always wins. |
231	| `eventParameters`, `queryParameters`, `pathParameters` | No | JSON objects of resolved values from Steps 3-4. Bucket each `parameters[]` entry by its `type`: `"query"` → `queryParameters` (e.g. GitHub `{"repo":"cli"}`, Outlook `{"sharedMailboxAddress":"..."}`), `"path"` → `pathParameters` (e.g. GitHub `{"owner":"uipath"}`), otherwise → `eventParameters`. Within each bucket, the key is `parameters[].name`. Each must be a JSON object. |
232	| `filter` | No | Structured filter tree — see [Filter Trees](#filter-trees) below. Omit to trigger on all events |
233	
234	The CLI computes the runtime JMESPath `filterExpression` from `filter` automatically and persists both into the workflow so Studio Web can re-open the trigger without losing the filter configuration. **Do not pass `filterExpression` directly — the validator rejects it.**
235	The command populates `inputs.detail` (including the internal `configuration` blob with the `filter` tree and combined `filterExpression`) and creates workflow-level connection bindings.
236	
237	> **Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file: `uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json`

239	### Step 6b — Retrieve and display webhook URL (webhooks only)
240	
241	Applies when `eventMode` is `"webhooks"`, regardless of `byoaConnection`.
242	
243	> **Guard:** If the trigger object's `isWebhookUrlVisible` is `false` (from Step 1b), skip this step — the connector manages webhook registration automatically and does not expose a URL. If you do not have `triggers objects` output, you skipped Step 1b — go back.
244	
245	Follow [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md — Webhook URL Retrieval](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#webhook-url-retrieval) for the exact commands (`uip is connections list` → `ElementInstanceId` → `uip is webhooks config`).
246	
247	**Presenting the URL:** If the Step 1b `triggers objects` response included `design.textBlocks`, use that text verbatim (substituting `{webhookUrl}`) — it carries connector-specific registration instructions. Otherwise, use a generic message instructing the user to register the URL in their external service's app settings (e.g., Slack Event Subscriptions, Salesforce Outbound Messages). The trigger will not fire until the URL is registered and verified.
248	
249	**On failure:** if `ElementInstanceId` is empty, the connection is the wrong type — verify the `byoaConnection` flag from Step 1b and switch to a BYOA connection if required. If `webhooks config` itself fails, ping the connection (`uip is connections ping`) and re-authenticate via `uip is connections edit` if unhealthy.

253	## Wait for events (`uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>`)
254	
255	A **Wait for events** node waits for an external event **mid-flow** instead of starting the flow ("wait for the approval reply", "wait until the Jira issue is Done"). Same connector event as a trigger — identical `eventParameters`, `filterFields`, `outputResponseDefinition`, `eventMode`, connection binding, reference resolution, filter trees. Apply Steps 1-6 above unchanged; only the deltas below differ.
256	
257	| Aspect | Connector **trigger** | **Wait for events** (mid-flow) |
258	|---|---|---|
259	| Node type | `uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>` | `uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>` |
260	| Position | Start node — replaces the manual trigger | Mid-flow — has an `input` port |
261	| Add | Step 5: [replace the manual trigger](../../editing-operations-cli.md#replace-manual-trigger-with-connector-trigger) | `node add` like an action node; do **NOT** remove the start node |
262	| Ports | in: — · out: `output` | in: `input` · out: `output`, `error` |
263	| Start trigger | Is the flow's trigger | Not a trigger — flow still needs its own start trigger |
264	| Discovery search | `... search "<svc>" trigger` | `... search "<svc>" event` |
265	| Config (Steps 1-4, 6) | Identical | Identical |
266	
267	Add and wire:
268	
269	```bash
270	uip maestro flow node add <PROJECT>.flow uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event> \
271	  --label "<LABEL>" --position 400,144 --output json
272	```
273	
274	Wire an incoming edge into `input` and an outgoing edge from `output` per [editing-operations-json.md — Insert a node between two existing nodes](../../editing-operations-json.md#insert-a-node-between-two-existing-nodes). Downstream reads `$vars.{eventNodeId}.output` (payload) and `$vars.{eventNodeId}.error`. Wire `error` only when the requirements say what an event-wait failure should do — otherwise leave it unwired and let the failure fault the flow ([file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles)).
275	
276	> **The flow still needs a separate start trigger.** A mid-flow event node does **not** start the flow. Do not remove `core.trigger.manual`/`scheduled` or the connector trigger that begins the flow.

280	## Filter Trees
281	
282	Filters are authored as a **structured tree**, not a string expression. The CLI compiles the tree into a JMESPath `filterExpression` using the same logic Studio Web does, and writes both forms into the flow so the trigger round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
283	
284	### Tree shape
285	
286	```jsonc
287	{
288	  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
289	  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
290	  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
291	    {
292	      "id": "<fieldName>",        // from filterFields.fields[].name
293	      "operator": "<Operator>",   // see operator table below
294	      "value": {
295	        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time
296	        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
297	        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not supported
298	      }
299	    }
300	  ],
301	  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
302	}
303	```
304	
305	A no-op filter — used when the user wants all events to fire the trigger — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
306	
307	### Supported operators
308	
309	| Operator | Meaning | Typical field types |
310	|---|---|---|
311	| `Equals` / `NotEquals` | Exact (in)equality | string, number, boolean |
312	| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | Numeric comparison | number, integer |
313	| `Contains` / `NotContains` | Substring match | string |
314	| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | Prefix / suffix match | string |
315	| `IsEmpty` / `IsNotEmpty` | Value is / is not empty string | string (no `value` needed) |
316	| `Is` / `IsNot` | Boolean is true / false | boolean (no `value` needed) |
317	| `In` / `NotIn` / `IsOneOf` / `IsNotOneOf` | Membership — pass comma-separated values in `value.value` | string, number |
318	| `Before` / `BeforeOrEqual` / `After` / `AfterOrEqual` / `DateTimeEquals` / `DateTimeNotEqual` | Date-time comparison (ISO-8601 strings) | date-time |
319	
320	### Examples
321	
322	**Emails containing "urgent" in the subject:**
323	
324	```json
325	{
326	  "groupOperator": 0,
327	  "index": 0,
328	  "filters": [
329	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
330	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
331	  ]
332	}
333	```
334	
335	**Emails from a specific sender AND subject contains "good day":**
336	
337	```json
338	{
339	  "groupOperator": 0,
340	  "index": 0,
341	  "filters": [
342	    { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
343	      "value": { "value": "boss@example.com", "rawString": "\"boss@example.com\"", "isLiteral": true } },
344	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
345	      "value": { "value": "good day", "rawString": "\"good day\"", "isLiteral": true } }
346	  ]
347	}
348	```
349	
350	**Multiple senders (OR) nested inside an outer AND with a subject match:**
351	
352	```json
353	{
354	  "groupOperator": 0,
355	  "index": 0,
356	  "filters": [
357	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
358	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
359	  ],
360	  "groups": [
361	    {
362	      "groupOperator": 1,
363	      "index": 1,
364	      "filters": [
365	        { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
366	          "value": { "value": "a@ex.com", "rawString": "\"a@ex.com\"", "isLiteral": true } },
367	        { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
368	          "value": { "value": "b@ex.com", "rawString": "\"b@ex.com\"", "isLiteral": true } }
369	      ]
370	    }
371	  ]
372	}
373	```
374	
375	### How to build a filter tree from `filterFields`
376	
377	1. Run `flow registry get` with `--connection-id` (Step 2) and read the `filterFields.fields` array. Each entry has a `name` (use as the leaf `id`), a `type` (drives operator selection), and an optional `description`.
378	
379	Then follow [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md > Building Filter Trees from filterFields](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#building-filter-trees-from-filterfields) for the rest of the procedure (operator selection, leaf composition, value wrapping), the mandatory-filter contract (connector-mandated values like Gmail folder go on `eventParameters`, never the freeform `filter` tree), and array-shaped field handling.
380	
381	### What NOT to generate
382	
383	| Invalid input | Why it fails | Valid replacement |
384	|---|---|---|
385	| `"filterExpression": "(contains(subject, 'x'))"` | Legacy format — the CLI now rejects `filterExpression` as an input field (see MST-8802). It is *only* an output in the generated `.flow`. | Build a `filter` tree with a `Contains` leaf. |
386	| `"filter": "(subject == 'x')"` | `filter` must be an object, not a string. | Structured tree with `filters: [...]`. |
387	| `{ "id": "fields.subject", ... }` | `fields.` prefix — use the bare field name from `filterFields.fields[].name`. | `{ "id": "subject", ... }` |
388	| `{ "id": "subject", "operator": "contains", ... }` | Operator is case-sensitive — use PascalCase. | `"operator": "Contains"` |
389	| `{ "value": "urgent" }` on a leaf | Bare string — must be wrapped in the `WorkflowValue` object. | `{ "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }` |
390	| `{ "isLiteral": false, "value": "${var}" }` | Expression values are not yet supported by the CLI port. | Resolve the value first, then pass it as a literal. |
391	| Adding a freeform leaf for a connector-mandated field (e.g. Gmail folder, Slack channelId) | Mandatory filters derived from connector event metadata are emitted automatically by the CLI from `eventParameters` — duplicating them in the freeform tree double-applies the clause. | Set the value through `eventParameters` only; the CLI AND-joins the mandatory JMES clause into the top-level `inputs.detail.filterExpression` (matching SW's `combinedFilterExpression`). It is *not* persisted on `essentialConfiguration` — SW classifies it optional and rebuilds it from input field values on restore. |

442	## Testing Trigger Flows
443	
444	`uip maestro flow debug` works with trigger-based flows. Debug does **not** wait for a live event — it **pulls the most recent matching event** from the connector's lookback window and executes immediately.
445	
446	### How debug works for triggers
447	
448	1. Debug calls the connector's `/events/debug` endpoint with `maxResults=5` and a `startDate` (default: 1 hour ago)
449	2. The connector returns up to 5 matching events from that window, sorted most-recent-first
450	3. The runtime uses `FilterMatches[0]` (the most recent match) as the trigger input
451	4. The flow executes immediately with that event data
452	5. If **no matching events** exist in the lookback window, debug fails with error code `3005` (TriggerNoMatches)
453	
454	```bash
455	uip maestro flow debug . --output json
456	# → Fetches most recent matching event from the past ~1 hour
457	# → Flow executes immediately with that event data
458	```
459	
460	### Polling vs webhook triggers in debug
461	
462	| Trigger mode | Debug support | Behavior |
463	|---|---|---|
464	| `polling` | Supported | Pulls recent events via debug API, executes immediately |
465	| `webhooks` | **Not supported** | Webhook triggers cannot be tested in Studio debug mode — debug requires Orchestrator |
466	
467	> **If the trigger uses `webhooks` event mode**, tell the user that debug is not available for webhook triggers. They must deploy to Orchestrator and test with a real webhook event.
468	
469	### Key differences from manual-trigger debug
470	
471	| Aspect | Manual trigger | Connector trigger (polling) |
472	|---|---|---|
473	| Execution start | Immediate with user-provided inputs | Immediate with most recent matching event |
474	| User action needed | Provide input values | Ensure a matching event exists in the past ~1 hour |
475	| Failure mode | Missing required inputs | No matching events in lookback window (error 3005) |
476	
477	### Pre-debug checklist
478	
479	1. **Verify the connection is healthy** — `uip is connections ping "<id>"`
480	2. **Confirm a matching event exists** — the user should have produced the event (e.g., sent an email, created a Jira issue) within the past hour
481	3. **Check event mode** — if `webhooks`, debug is not supported; inform the user
482

484	
485	## Debug
486	
487	### Common Errors
488	
489	| Error | Cause | Fix |
490	|---|---|---|
491	| `Trigger nodes require --connection-id` | Ran `registry get` without `--connection-id` | Re-run with `--connection-id <id>` — required for all trigger nodes |
492	| `Invalid --detail` saying `objectName is required for the trigger` — or, on older CLIs, an opaque `Error configuring node` / `Response returned an error code` on every `--detail` shape | The trigger is **generic** (`activityType: "GenericTrigger"`, e.g. Data Fabric `record-created`): its manifest ships the `objectName` context entry without a value, and configure needs the object to fetch trigger metadata. Older CLIs rejected `objectName` as a `--detail` key and called the metadata API with an empty object name — hence the opaque server error. | Pass the object in `--detail.objectName` (resolve it per Step 1b-2). On an older CLI that rejects the key, `Edit` the trigger **definition's** `model.context` `objectName` entry to add `"value": "<object>"`, then re-run `node configure`. Curated triggers never need this — their manifest carries the objectName. |
493	| No trigger nodes in registry | Not authenticated or registry not pulled | Run `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
494	| Connection not found in bindings | `node configure` not run or connection expired | Re-run `node configure` with valid `connectionId` and `folderKey` |
495	| Event parameter missing at runtime | Required event parameter not configured (commonly one returned by `triggers describe` but absent from `triggers objects → parameters[]`) | Re-run **both** `uip is triggers objects` (Step 1b) **and** `uip is triggers describe` (Step 1b-2). Configure every field marked `required` in **either** `parameters[]` or `EventParameters` (resolving references) under the correct `--detail` bucket. |
496	| `filterExpression is derived from the filter tree and cannot be provided directly` | Passed `filterExpression` string instead of a `filter` tree | Build a structured `filter` tree — see [Filter Trees](#filter-trees) |
497	| Trigger fires on events the filter should exclude; `node configure` reported Success | A leaf `id` does not match any `filterFields.fields[].name` (matching is case-sensitive). The CLI drops the unmatched leaf from the compiled `filterExpression` instead of failing | Re-run `registry get --connection-id <id>`, compare every leaf `id` against `filterFields.fields[].name`, then re-run `node configure` with the exact names |
498	| Trigger not firing | Event parameters point to wrong resource (e.g., wrong folder ID) | Re-resolve reference fields with `uip is resources run list` |
499	| Trigger faults immediately with no visible error after a clean build | Event parameter uses a reference ID scoped to a **different** connection (common when copying from a prior flow in the same session — e.g., a `parentFolderId` for mailbox A pasted into a trigger bound to mailbox B's connection) | Re-run `uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID>`, extract the fresh ID, update `eventParameters` in `--detail`, re-run `node configure`, re-debug. See Step 3 and the top-level Anti-Pattern on reference-ID reuse in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md). |
500	| Definition's `model.context` missing operation | Definition not copied correctly, or node added before registry pull | Re-run `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`, then verify the `definitions[]` entry contains `model.context` with `connectorKey`/`operation`/`objectName` as returned by `registry get` |
501	| Trigger faults at runtime with webhook-related error | Standard (non-BYOA) connection used for a trigger that requires `byoaConnection: true` | Run `uip is triggers objects` (Step 1b) to check `byoaConnection` flag, then switch to a BYOA connection with `uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --output json`. If no BYOA connections exist, user must create one. |
502	| `connections list` returns empty but connections exist in the IS portal | CLI is using cached connection data that is stale | Retry with `--refresh` flag: `uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --refresh --output json` |
503	| `ElementInstanceId` is empty on the selected connection | Connection is not a BYOA connection, or connector does not support webhooks on this connection type | Verify the trigger requires BYOA (Step 1b `byoaConnection` flag). If `true`, switch to a BYOA connection. |
504	
505	### Debug Tips
506	
507	1. **Always verify the connection is healthy** before debugging trigger issues — run `uip is connections ping "<id>"`
508	2. **`flow validate` does NOT catch trigger-specific issues** — missing event parameters, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime
509	3. **Event parameters with `reference` objects** need resolved IDs, not display names — same as IS activity fields
510	4. **Filters are optional** — omit `filter` from `--detail` if the user wants all events to trigger the flow. Do not invent an "empty" expression.
511	5. **Bindings are auto-managed** — `node configure` creates flow-level bindings; `flow debug`/packaging generates `bindings_v2.json` from them
512	6. **Use `uip maestro flow node remove` to remove the manual trigger** — do NOT use `Edit` to delete the start node. The CLI automatically removes associated edges, orphaned definitions, and regenerates `variables.nodes`. Hand-editing skips these cleanup steps and can leave orphaned references.
513	7. **Check `outputResponseDefinition` before writing downstream expressions** — trigger output field names vary by connector. Do not assume field names like `.text` or `.subject` — verify from the enriched `registry get` response (Step 2)
514	8. **Validate filter field names against `filterFields` yourself** — only field names returned in `filterFields.fields[].name` are valid leaf `id`s in the filter tree, and matching is case-sensitive. The CLI no longer rejects an unknown field at configure time: it drops that leaf from the compiled `filterExpression` and reports Success. A guessed name therefore surfaces as a trigger that fires on events the filter should exclude, not as an error.

18	  --label "<LABEL>" \

77

79	uip maestro flow edge remove <ProjectName>.flow <EDGE_ID>
80	uip maestro flow edge remove <ProjectName>.flow <EDGE_ID> --output json
81	```
82	
83	### List edges
84	
85	```bash
86	uip maestro flow edge list <ProjectName>.flow --output json
87	```
88	
89	Returns all edges with `id`, `sourceNodeId`, `sourcePort`, `targetNodeId`, `targetPort`.
90	
91	### Configure a connector node
92	
93	After adding a connector node with `node add`, configure it with connection details:
94	
95	```bash
96	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> \
97	  --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>'
98	```
99	
100	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
101	- Populates `inputs.detail` (connectionId, method, endpoint, bodyParameters, etc.)
102	- Creates connection binding entries in `bindings_v2.json`
103	- Creates connection resource files under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
104	
105	The `--detail` JSON schema differs between connector activity nodes, connector trigger nodes, and managed HTTP nodes — see [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), and [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md) for the exact fields.
106	
107	**Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file:
108	
109	```bash
110	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json
111	```
112	
113	### Configure a managed HTTP node
114	
115	After adding a `core.action.http.v2` node, configure it with target connector and connection details:
116	
117	```bash
118	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> \
119	  --detail '{
120	    "authentication": "connector",
121	    "targetConnector": "<TARGET_CONNECTOR_KEY>",
122	    "connectionId": "<TARGET_CONNECTION_ID>",
123	    "folderKey": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
124	    "method": "GET",
125	    "path": "/api/endpoint",
126	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
127	  }'
128	```
129	
130	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
131	- Wraps your fields into the full `inputs.detail` structure (connector: `uipath-uipath-http`, bodyParameters, configuration)
132	- Generates `bindings_v2.json` with the target connector's connection
133	- Creates a connection resource file under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
134	
135	See [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md) for the full configuration workflow and JSON structure.
136	
137	### Validate
138	
139	```bash
140	uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
141	```
142	
143	Run **once** after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## Carve-Out Composite Operations
148	
149	These combine primitives only for workflows that are themselves carve-outs. Do not use them for non-carve-out structural edits; use [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) instead.
150	
151	### Replace manual trigger with connector trigger
152	
153	1. Remove the manual trigger (also removes its edges and orphaned definition):
154	   ```bash
155	   uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow start --output json
156	   ```
157	2. Add the connector trigger node:
158	   ```bash
159	   uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow <TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE> \
160	     --label "<LABEL>" --position 200,144 --output json
161	   ```
162	3. Re-wire edge from the new trigger to the next node:
163	   ```bash
164	   uip maestro flow edge add <ProjectName>.flow <NEW_TRIGGER_ID> <NEXT_NODE_ID> \
165	     --source-port output --target-port input --output json
166	   ```
167	4. Configure the trigger with connection and event parameters:
168	   ```bash
169	   uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NEW_TRIGGER_ID> --detail '<TRIGGER_DETAIL_JSON>'
170	   ```
171	
172	See [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md) for the full `--detail` schema.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## Operations Not Supported by CLI
177	
178	These operations require the `Edit` tool. Use the [Edit / Write strategy guide](editing-operations-json.md) for:
179	
180	1. **Any non-carve-out structural edit** — node/edge CRUD, scheduled triggers, HITL QuickForm nodes, inline-agent nodes, non-connector resources, and graph rewiring
181	2. **Node input updates** — the CLI does not have a `node update` command; use `Edit` to preserve node IDs and `$vars.{nodeId}` references
182	3. **Workflow variables** — add/remove/update `variables.globals`
183	4. **Variable updates** — add/modify `variables.variableUpdates` entries
184	5. **Output mapping on End nodes** — add `outputs` object with `source` expressions
185	6. **Subflows** — create `subflows.{nodeId}` with nested nodes, edges, variables

136:> **`<objectName>` is the activity's API object name, not the node-type's trailing segment — and NOT a case-conversion of it.** Read it from the node definition copied into `definitions[]` by `node add`: `model.context[]` entry `{name:"objectName", value:"…"}` (or the `objectName` field inside the `configuration` `=jsonString:` blob). Never derive it by transforming the node-type suffix — kebab→snake (`send-email` → `send_email`) and kebab→Pascal are both guesses and both 404. Example: node type `…google-gmail.send-email` has objectName `SendEmail` (not `send_email`); `…teams.send-bot-direct-message` has objectName `bot_direct_messages` (not `send-bot-direct-message`). A 404 means wrong objectName — re-read it from the definition and retry; do NOT treat the 404 as "describe unavailable" and skip the step. Skipping describe loses `requestFields[].reference.filterPattern` and other IS-level metadata that `registry get` does not carry (see Step 4).
138:> **Sequence, don't parallelize, the objectName-dependent calls.** `<objectName>` is an OUTPUT of `node add` (it lands in `definitions[]`). Read that value before calling `is resources describe` — do not place `describe` in the same parallel Bash batch as `node add` or `registry get`, or you'll have nothing to pass but a guess. This is the failure mode behind the snake-case 404 above.
142:- **`parameters`** — query and path parameters (may include required params not in `requestFields`, e.g. `send_as` for Slack). Parameters carry `reference` objects too — scan them in Step 4 exactly like body fields.
143:- **`requestFields`** — body fields with `name`, `type`, `required`, `description`, and `reference` objects for ID resolution. Pair these field names with the `path` above (e.g. `messageToSend` for Slack `/send_message_to_channel_v2`).
148:**Run whenever the activity has a parent-field-driven schema** — an api-type ObjectAction in `objectActions[]` or `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (see Step 6c's support table). Applies to **every** operation with such an action — Create/Edit/Update for parent-driven required body fields AND Get/Retrieve/Query for the response-schema fields downstream nodes will reference. The base `describe` returns only static metadata; this step runs the matching ObjectAction against the live connection so the cache you author in Step 6c is a replay of a real call, not a fabrication.
158:Check **BOTH `requestFields` AND `parameters`** from the metadata for entries with a `reference` object — these require ID lookup from the connector's live data. Use `uip is resources run list` to resolve them:
160:> **References are NOT body-field-only.** Query and path parameters carry `reference` objects too, and on some connectors the activity's PRIMARY input is a required **path parameter** whose `reference` is the design-time lookup behind a Studio Web dropdown. Scanning only `requestFields` misses it — the node then configures and passes `flow validate` with an unverified value and 404s at runtime. The same `reference` blocks appear on `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` in `registry get` output (with or without `--connection-id`) — when projecting parameter metadata for inspection, always include the `reference` key, not just `name`/`required`/`design.component`.

Primitive `.flow` mutations: node/edge CRUD, variables, output mappings.

Each subcommand touches every array the operation implies (nodes, edges, definitions,
variables.nodes, variables.variableUpdates, layout.nodes) in one pass and writes the file
back with 2-space indent.

positional arguments:

    add-node            insert a node + definition + variables.nodes + layout
                        entry
    delete-node         remove a node and cascade
                        edges/variables/updates/layout/definition
    add-edge            add an edge with both ports; sets errorHandlingEnabled
                        for error edges
    delete-edge         remove an edge by id or by endpoints
    set-input           in-place inputs update (dotted key path), preserves
                        node id
    add-variable        declare a workflow variable in variables.globals
    add-output-mapping  map an out variable on an End/terminate node
    add-variable-update

The flow is built and validated successfully. Summary:

**File:** `/work/output/artifacts/skill-flow-ixp-routing/contracts/ContractProcessingSolution/ContractApprovalFlow/ContractApprovalFlow.flow`

**Topology** (trigger → download → extract → approve → decide → end):
1. **New Contract PDF Uploaded** — Google Drive "File Created" connector trigger, filtered to `.pdf` extension, polling My Drive
2. **Download Contract PDF** — Google Drive "Download File" connector activity, bound to the triggered file's ID
3. **Extract Contract Fields** — real published IXP node (`employment-agreements-d4ee40a0-ixp` model), `fileRef` wired to the downloaded file; extracts party names, effective date, and termination clause as part of its trained field taxonomy
4. **Approve Contract Extraction** — inline HITL quick-form showing the extracted fields, with Approve/Reject outcomes
5. **Approved?** decision node branching on the human's decision → **Contract Approved** / **Contract Rejected** End nodes

**Validation:** `flow validate` (run once, as instructed) returned `Status: "Valid"` with one benign warning (the Drive trigger and download activity share one connection — intentional, since both need the same account). `flow format` ran afterward and fixed layout/sizing.

One caveat: the IXP model I used (`employment-agreements-d4ee40a0-ixp`) is the closest published extraction model available on this tenant — no generic "contract" model exists, so the exact taxonomy field names for party names/effective date/termination clause weren't confirmed (the taxonomy lookup command needs a differently-named IXP project than what's in the flow registry, and didn't resolve). The HITL node's field bindings reference the extraction's `Fields[]` array generically rather than specific field names — this would need tightening once the real taxonomy is confirmed.

task_config.source_yaml:
task_id: skill-flow-ixp-routing
description: >
  IxP routing (positive) — document-extraction build prompts fanned out via
  `dataset.rows`. Each row carries a distinct user prompt; success criteria are
  identical across all rows.

  Scope: did the agent route to the IxP plugin, not did the flow work.
  Assertions verify the agent ran the right CLI-command patterns (registry
  search for uipath.ixp.*) and landed a uipath.ixp.* or core.logic.mock node —
  NOT whether the resulting flow is correct or would execute.

  Failure here is signal about SKILL.md or the IxP Plugin Index entry —
  do NOT relax assertions; feed findings back in.

  Rows are phrased as greenfield builds because the sandbox seeds no `.flow`.
  A prompt claiming "I have a UiPath Flow" makes the agent rightly decline to
  attach a node to a project that does not exist.

tags: [uipath-maestro-flow, integration, mode:build, lifecycle:generate, node:ixp]
dataset:
  rows:
    - id: explicit
      prompt: >-
        Build a UiPath Flow with an IXP node that reads PDF invoices from a
        SharePoint folder and extracts the structured fields so the next step
        can post them to SAP.

    - id: invoice-extraction
      prompt: >-
        Build a UiPath Flow that pulls vendor name, invoice number, invoice
        date, total amount, and line items out of PDF invoices saved in a
        SharePoint folder, then posts the result to our accounting system.

    - id: receipts
      prompt: >-
        Add a document-extraction step to my flow that reads receipt images
        from a folder and pulls out merchant, date, and total.

    - id: contracts
      prompt: >-
        Build a flow that extracts party names, effective date, and the
        termination clause from PDF contracts, then routes them to an approval
        step.

    - id: forms-classify
      prompt: >-
        Build a Maestro flow with an IxP node that classifies incoming PDF
        forms and extracts their fields before the next step.

initial_prompt: |
  ${row.prompt}

  Important:
  - The `uip` CLI is already available.
  - Use `--output json` on all uip commands.
  - Work inside the stated working directory — do NOT `cd` to a parent.
  - Do NOT run `uip maestro flow debug` or `uip maestro flow deploy`.
  - Run `uip maestro flow validate` at most ONCE. If it fails, stop.
  - Do NOT iterate on validation errors or rewrite the flow to fix them. A broken flow is acceptable.
  - You do not need a working flow — a skeleton whose nodes cover the steps of the request is enough. Leave a node unconfigured rather than leaving a step out.

success_criteria:
  # What this checks: did the agent search the registry for IxP nodes?
  # Passes (case-insensitive) when the agent ran either:
  #   • `registry list`                   — list all nodes, or
  #   • `registry search|list|get <term>` — <term> contains ixp / document / extract
  #                                         (prefix match, so extract → extraction)
  # routing_listing.yaml drops `get` (read-only). Keep in sync with
  # scaffold_minimal.yaml, scaffold_multinode.yaml, routing_listing.yaml.
  - type: command_executed
    description: "Agent searched the registry for IxP node types"
    tool_name: "Bash"
    command_pattern: '(?i)uip\s+maestro\s+flow\s+registry\s+(list\b|(search|list|get)\b[^\n]*\b(ixp|document|extract))'
    min_count: 1
    suite_thresholds: {mean: 0.85}

  # Greps the actual .flow artifact rather than the command stream — the
  # command_executed checker truncates tool params at 2000 chars, which hides
  # `"type": "core.logic.mock"` when the agent writes a large flow file in a
  # single Write call.  Per references/plugins/ixp/impl.md, the agent must land
  # either an `uipath.ixp.*` node or a `core.logic.mock` placeholder.
  - type: run_command
    description: "Agent added an IxP or core.logic.mock placeholder node to a .flow file (per references/plugins/ixp/impl.md)"
    command: 'grep -rqE "\"type\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"(uipath\.ixp|core\.logic\.mock)" --include="*.flow" .'
    expected_exit_code: 0
    suite_thresholds: {mean: 0.85}

run_limits:
  max_turns: 80
  task_timeout: 900
